nodes.What it is: A simulator repeatedly computes forces, accelerations and the next state. The time step and numerical integrator decide how much error accumulates, even before the robot touches anything.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Forward dynamics remains foundational; compare energy drift and wall-clock cost before trusting faster rollouts. Simulator speed claims depend on model, batch size and hardware. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A CPU laptop is enough to plot numerical errors and film a toy scene.

nodes.What it is: Collision geometry tells the engine which shapes can touch; it is often simpler than the visible mesh. A contact solver estimates the forces that stop objects passing through one another, using approximations to friction and compliance.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Soft-contact and hybrid-contact models make different compromises. Newton and MuJoCo offer current implementations; matching a visually plausible stack is not proof of accurate friction or impact. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Google DeepMind; MIT Drake; Newton community
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simple sliding and stacking scenes reveal contact errors without building a robot.

nodes.Node: Robot and scene formats: URDF, MJCF, SDF & USD
nodes.What it is: Robot descriptions store links, joints, masses and collision shapes; scene formats also organize environments and assets. URDF, MJCF, SDF and USD serve different workflows, so converting a file can silently lose physics settings.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: USD supports composition of large scenes, while MJCF includes engine-specific dynamics settings. Validate joint limits, inertias, scale and collision geometry after every importer; visual equivalence is insufficient. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ROS community; Google DeepMind; OpenUSD; Gazebo
nodes._accessibility_reason: Editing small text models fits software skills and needs no hardware.

nodes.What it is: A bridge lets ROS 2 software exchange commands and sensor messages with a simulated robot. Simulation time must reach every node consistently, or apparently valid messages can be too old or from the wrong clock.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Gazebo Harmonic has a maintained ROS 2 bridge workflow. Use a supported ROS/Gazebo pairing and pin versions; Gazebo Classic tutorials are not drop-in instructions for modern Gazebo. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Official bridge tutorials provide a starting point, but middleware and version pairing add setup work.

nodes.What it is: Virtual cameras, depth sensors and inertial sensors turn simulator state into the measurements a robot would receive. The engine can also provide exact labels, but perfect labels and clean images can hide problems found on real sensors.
nodes.Prerequisites: Camera geometry; arrays; basic sensor noise
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ManiSkill supports parallel visual data collection and Isaac Sim Replicator supports synthetic data workflows. Include noise, clipping, missing depth, timestamp errors and calibration rather than equating photorealism with sensor truth. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: RGB and depth demos are accessible; photorealistic rendering may require a suitable GPU.

nodes.What it is: Instead of running one world at a time, a GPU can step many copies together. A vectorized environment batches actions, observations and resets, making large robot-learning experiments practical.
nodes.Prerequisites: Python arrays; GPU memory; environment reset API
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MJX, MuJoCo Playground, Isaac Lab, ManiSkill and Genesis provide parallel workflows with different backends. Opened current docs show Isaac Lab multi-backend support and Playground evolving toward Warp; pin a revision rather than assuming older tutorials still match. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Google DeepMind; NVIDIA; ManiSkill; Genesis AI
nodes._accessibility_reason: The batching concepts are familiar, but GPU access and backend compatibility can block the first run.

nodes.What it is: Domain randomization changes lighting, geometry or physical parameters between simulated trials. The aim is robustness to uncertainty, not simply making many colorful images.
nodes.Prerequisites: Train/test splits; parameter distributions; basic evaluation
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Visual randomization has established primary evidence, but a wider distribution can also make learning harder. Treat the LeRobot low-cost transfer wedge as a hypothesis: estimate realistic ranges and reserve unseen combinations for evaluation. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Randomization and held-out evaluation fit AI skills and can start entirely in simulation.

nodes.What it is: System identification estimates unknown physical parameters from measured motion. Calibrating a simulator means checking that its masses, friction, delays and actuator behavior predict observations not used during fitting.
nodes.Prerequisites: Regression; time series; safe joint operation for real trials
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Contact and actuator parameters may compensate for one another, so a good training fit can be misleading. Begin with identifiable toy models and held-out trajectories before adjusting an entire robot. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: MIT Drake; Google DeepMind; LeRobot community
nodes._accessibility_reason: Offline fitting is approachable; real calibration needs careful synchronization and safe excitation.

nodes.What it is: A digital twin reconstructs a particular real workspace for repeatable experiments. Gaussian splatting can reproduce how that workspace looks from new viewpoints, but rendering primitives do not automatically provide collision geometry or material physics.
nodes.Prerequisites: Multi-view geometry; camera calibration; contact simulation
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The 2025 real-to-sim soft-body evaluation paper couples physics-informed reconstruction and Gaussian rendering. Its reported policy correlations are task-specific evidence, not proof that any photorealistic twin predicts real success. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Real-to-Sim Robot Policy Evaluation authors; SimplerEnv authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Capturing, aligning and validating appearance plus physics is substantially harder than loading a ready-made scene.

nodes.What it is: A learned simulator predicts future observations from past observations and actions instead of solving all physics equations. Its predictions can be useful for testing, but plausible videos can still ignore an action or invent physically impossible outcomes.
nodes.Prerequisites: Deep learning; sequence models; held-out rollouts
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DreamerV3 supplies a reproducible latent-model baseline; the 2026 BWM paper proposes action-conditioned robotic simulation. Validate action sensitivity, state consistency and error growth, not just image scores; no universal substitute for physics is established here. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: DreamerV3 authors; Boundless World Model authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Small latent-model experiments are feasible; large video simulators have uncertain compute and access costs.

nodes.What it is: A benchmark defines tasks, resets, success rules and reporting so experiments can be compared. A simulation score is evidence about those settings, not a certificate of real-world competence.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ManiSkill, RoboCasa and SimplerEnv cover complementary task and transfer-evaluation settings. Keep assets, seeds, horizons, success criteria and reset rules fixed; report failed runs and avoid leaking evaluation conditions into training. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Existing task suites enable immediate measurement, though fair protocol design takes discipline.

nodes.Node: Procedural scenes, asset pipelines & task generation
nodes.What it is: Procedural generation creates varied environments from reusable rules and assets. Useful robot scenes need valid scales, collision shapes and reachable task states, not merely attractive layouts.
nodes.Prerequisites: Scene graphs; geometry; random seeds; asset licenses
nodes.Frontier state 2026: RoboCasa provides large-scale household environments and Isaac Sim Replicator supports variation. Generated tasks require solvability and collision checks plus license provenance; quantity alone does not guarantee useful diversity. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Python scene generation gives fast visual feedback; quality filters matter more than buying hardware.

nodes.What it is: Differentiable simulation computes how changing a parameter or action changes a later outcome. Those gradients can help optimization, but collisions and changing contact modes can make them unstable or misleading.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Warp offers differentiable kernels and Newton emphasizes extensible GPU physics. Brax now recommends MJX or MuJoCo Warp for simulation, so use current maintained backends; differentiability does not imply every solver or contact case has useful gradients. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Gradient tooling fits AI skills, but physically meaningful derivatives through contact need mathematical care.

nodes.What it is: Deformable simulators model objects that bend or flow rather than staying rigid. Cloth, soft solids and particles require different approximations, and coupling them to rigid robots can be expensive and sensitive to settings.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Genesis describes a multiphysics platform; Newton and Isaac Lab expose additional solver workflows. This node concerns simulation fidelity and coupling, not the manipulation pilot node about learning to handle deformable objects. Snapshot of opened references, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Genesis AI; Newton community; NVIDIA; real-to-sim evaluation authors
nodes._accessibility_reason: Ready-made examples are runnable, but identifying material parameters and validating coupling is difficult.
